name: Congenital Amegakaryocytic Thrombocytopenia with MPL Mutation

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Congenital Amegakaryocytic Thrombocytopenia

criteria.description: Severe thrombocytopenia present at birth or early infancy
Bone marrow biopsy showing absence or severe reduction of megakaryocytes
Identification of pathogenic mutation in the MPL gene
Exclusion of other causes of thrombocytopenia and bone marrow failure

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of severe thrombocytopenia at birth or early infancy, bone marrow amegakaryocytosis, and confirmed MPL gene mutation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is essential for definitive diagnosis.

common.symptomName: Abnormal form of the vertebral bodies

laboratory: Severe thrombocytopenia with platelet counts typically <20,000/µL
Normal or reduced white blood cell and red blood cell counts in early stages
Bone marrow biopsy showing absent or severely reduced megakaryocytes
imaging: Neuroimaging (CT/MRI) may show intracranial hemorrhage in severe bleeding cases
other: Progressive bone marrow failure leading to pancytopenia

distinguishingFeatures: Normal bone marrow megakaryocytes or increased

redFlags: Severe bleeding in neonate or infant
Rapid progression to bone marrow failure
references: Ballmaier M, Germeshausen M. Congenital amegakaryocytic thrombocytopenia: clinical and molecular aspects. Haematologica. 2009;94(3):326-329.
Germeshausen M, Ballmaier M. Congenital thrombocytopenias: new insights into megakaryocyte maturation and platelet formation. Hematology Am Soc Hematol Educ Program. 2012;2012:38-44.
